ei.title: The Risks of Purpose-Washing in Branding
ei.subject: 6월_2026 고2 모의고사
ei.lesson: The Risks of Purpose-Washing in Branding

fullPassage: Realising the benefits of differentiation, some brands broadcast their social purpose before they do much actual good. Their marketers are using social purpose to boost the brand's reputation, rather than embracing the purpose itself. Making a real difference with social problems is hard enough; to succeed, it has to follow from an authentic, company-wide commitment to the purpose. Otherwise the mission is just window-dressing, or what we call "purpose-washing" — similar to green-washing, where purpose-driven activities serve mainly for publicity purposes. We end up with what Anand Giridhardas describes in Winners Take All: "social purpose that just furthers the charade of elites disrupting the old order without giving much back". Purpose-washing brands gain one of the benefits of social purpose, differentiation, but only for a short while. They lose out on positioning for future markets, and they might even make employees feel worse about working for them.

questions.passage: Realising the benefits of differentiation, some brands (A)[broadcast / conceal] their social purpose before they do much actual good. Their marketers are using social purpose to (B)[boost / diminish] the brand's reputation, rather than embracing the purpose itself. Making a real difference with social problems is hard enough; to succeed, it has to follow from an (C)[authentic / superficial], company-wide commitment to the purpose. Otherwise the mission is just window-dressing, or what we call "purpose-washing" — similar to green-washing, where purpose-driven activities serve mainly for publicity purposes. We end up with what Anand Giridhardas describes in Winners Take All: "social purpose that just furthers the charade of elites disrupting the old order without giving much back". Purpose-washing brands gain one of the benefits of social purpose, differentiation, but only for a short while. They lose out on positioning for future markets, and they might even make employees feel worse about working for them.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: ① (A) broadcast(알리다) (B) boost(높이다) (C) authentic(진정한) 원문 그대로
det.analysis:
✅ ① broadcast(알리다) + boost(높이다) + authentic(진정한) ← 정답: 원문 그대로의 조합
❌ ② conceal(숨기다)은 broadcast(알리다)의 반의어
❌ ③ diminish(줄이다)은 boost(높이다)의 반의어
❌ ④ conceal(숨기다) + diminish(줄이다) + superficial(피상적인) 모두 원문과 반대

questions.passage: Realising the benefits of differentiation, some brands broadcast their social purpose before they do much actual good. Their marketers are using social purpose to boost the brand's reputation, rather than (A)[embracing / rejecting] the purpose itself. Making a real difference with social problems is hard enough; to succeed, it has to follow from an authentic, company-wide (B)[commitment / indifference] to the purpose. Otherwise the mission is just window-dressing, or what we call "purpose-washing" — similar to green-washing, where purpose-driven activities serve mainly for (C)[publicity / secrecy] purposes. We end up with what Anand Giridhardas describes in Winners Take All: "social purpose that just furthers the charade of elites disrupting the old order without giving much back". Purpose-washing brands gain one of the benefits of social purpose, differentiation, but only for a short while. They lose out on positioning for future markets, and they might even make employees feel worse about working for them.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: ④ (A) embracing(수용하다) (B) commitment(헌신) (C) publicity(홍보) 원문 그대로
det.analysis:
❌ ① rejecting(거부하다)은 embracing(수용하다)의 반의어로 부적절
❌ ② indifference(무관심)는 commitment(헌신)의 반의어로 부적절
❌ ③ secrecy(비밀)는 publicity(홍보)의 반의어로 부적절
✅ ④ embracing(수용하다) + commitment(헌신) + publicity(홍보) ← 정답: 원문 그대로의 조합

questions.passage: Realising the benefits of (A)[differentiation / uniformity], some brands broadcast their social purpose before they do much actual good. Their marketers are using social purpose to boost the brand's reputation, rather than embracing the purpose itself. Making a real difference with social problems is hard enough; to succeed, it has to follow from an authentic, company-wide commitment to the purpose. Otherwise the mission is just window-dressing, or what we call "purpose-washing" — similar to green-washing, where purpose-driven activities serve mainly for publicity purposes. We end up with what Anand Giridhardas describes in Winners Take All: "social purpose that just (B)[furthers / hinders] the charade of elites (C)[disrupting / maintaining] the old order without giving much back". They lose out on positioning for future markets, and they might even make employees feel worse about working for them.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: ④ (A) differentiation(차별화) (B) furthers(촉진하다) (C) disrupting(파괴하다) 원문 그대로
det.analysis:
❌ ① hinders(방해하다) ≠ furthers(촉진하다)
❌ ② uniformity(획일성) ≠ differentiation(차별화)
❌ ③ maintaining(유지하다) ≠ disrupting(파괴하다)
✅ ④ differentiation + furthers + disrupting ← 정답

questions.passage:

questions.stem: 다음 (A)와 (B)의 밑줄 친 broadcast가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: ① (A) 방송하다/알리다 (B) (씨를) 뿌리다: broadcast의 두 가지 뜻
det.analysis:
✅ ① (A) 방송하다 — 미디어를 통해 알리다 / (B) 뿌리다 — 씨앗을 고르게 뿌리다 ← 정답
❌ ② 의미 역전
❌ ③ 둘 다 방송하다 — (B)는 농업 맥락
❌ ④ 둘 다 뿌리다 — (A)는 미디어 맥락
det.tip: broadcast: ① (정보를) 방송하다/널리 알리다 ② (씨앗을) 뿌리다

✅ ③ elites: 엘리트/지배층 ← 정답
❌ ④ alternatives: 대안들 — 영영 정의와 무관

questions.passage: Their marketers are using social purpose to boost the brand's reputation, rather than __________ (embrace) the purpose itself. Making a real difference with social problems is hard enough; to succeed, it has to follow from an authentic, company-wide commitment to the purpose.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: embracing: embrace(동사, 포용하다)의 동명사형 → rather than 뒤에 동명사
det.analysis: embrace(동사) → embracing(동명사): rather than + V-ing 구문. rather than using과 병렬 구조이므로 동명사 embracing이 적절

questions.passage: Realising the benefits of differentiation, some brands broadcast their social purpose before they do much actual good. Their marketers are using social purpose to boost the brand's reputation, rather than embracing the purpose itself. Making a real difference with social problems is hard enough; to succeed, it has to follow from an authentic, company-wide commitment to the purpose. Otherwise the mission is just __________, or what we call "purpose-washing" — similar to green-washing, where purpose-driven activities serve mainly for publicity purposes. We end up with what Anand Giridhardas describes in Winners Take All: "social purpose that just furthers the charade of elites disrupting the old order without giving much back". Purpose-washing brands gain one of the benefits of social purpose, differentiation, but only for a short while. They lose out on positioning for future markets, and they might even make employees feel worse about working for them.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: ① window-dressing(겉치장): 사명이 그저 겉치장에 불과하다는 문맥
det.analysis:
✅ ① window-dressing: 겉치장 — 진정성 없는 겉모습 꾸미기 ← 정답
❌ ② problem-solving: 문제 해결 — 문맥상 부적절
❌ ③ decision-making: 의사결정 — 문맥상 부적절
❌ ④ record-breaking: 기록적인 — 문맥상 부적절
det.tip: window-dressing=겉치장/분식(실제 내용 없이 겉만 꾸미는 것)

det.korean: ④ purpose-driven(목적 주도의): 목적 주도 활동이 주로 홍보 목적으로 사용된다는 문맥
det.analysis:
❌ ① profit-driven: 이윤 주도의 — 문맥에서 social purpose 관련이므로 부적절
❌ ② customer-driven: 고객 주도의 — 문맥상 부적절
❌ ③ market-driven: 시장 주도의 — 문맥상 부적절
✅ ④ purpose-driven: 목적 주도의 ← 정답
